subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Frequency Modulation (FM)
description: A quick win: understand Frequency Modulation (FM).

hook.text: FM radio varies the frequency of the carrier instead of its amplitude. Same loudness, shifting pitch.

buildup.text: When the audio signal is loud, the carrier frequency swings widely. Quiet signals swing less.

discovery.text: FM is much more resistant to noise than AM because noise mostly affects amplitude, not frequency.

twist.text: FM uses more bandwidth than AM — the wide frequency swing needs a bigger channel allocation.

climax.text: FM radio delivers high-fidelity stereo music — far better audio quality than AM.

punchline.text: Shift the frequency, not the amplitude — FM trades bandwidth for clarity.

quiz.question: Why is FM more resistant to noise than AM?
options: Noise primarily affects amplitude, which FM ignores since information is in the frequency
FM operates at frequencies where noise doesn't exist
